title: Clarity Sprint and Risk Thermostat
redwood_attendees: Priya Nair - VP of Customer Success
customer_attendees: Several remote offices: US / EU / APAC
topics: Product prioritization: Dedicated vs Private features
summary: Leila opened with a short, candid review of Q1 performance and a moderated Q&A about tradeoffs for the next quarter. Leadership announced a measured hiring pause, clarified prioritization between Dedicated and Private investments, and committed to a cross-functional action plan to reduce on-call load. The conversation surfaced concerns about runway, enterprise sales timelines, and the need for tighter cost/latency narratives for customers.
action_items: Marco: produce 2-page reliability runbook and incident TL;DR for customers - due 2027-04-08
Rachel: re-scope Q2 roadmap to show clear M/M and M/V options for Dedicated vs Private - due 2027-04-12
Priya: compile top 8 enterprise security/RFP asks and update security kit - due 2027-04-09
Owen: design temporary on-call rotation relief and hire two short-term SRE contractors - due 2027-04-15
next_steps: Leila to share updated financial run-rate assumptions and headscount plan by next Friday
All product leads to join a Tuesday working session for roadmap triage (calendar invite sent)
Customer Success to prioritize 3 deals for Q2 push with tailored performance benchmarks
transcript: [00:00] Leila: Morning everyone, uh thanks for joining the company sync. It's... it's a bit of a different tone today. we want to be transparent about Q1 and what that means for the org.
full_transcript_body:
[00:22] Sanjay: I'll jump in with a quick tech pulse. Systems were stable overall but we had two P99 spikes during the rolling kernel tests and that leaked into some customer tail latencies, we fixed the gating but it cost ops time.
[00:45] Marco: Yeah, that was the cascade I was worried about. We have recurring pressure on our long-sequence models when batching and cache warmups collide. not an easy one.
[01:10] Rachel: From product side we saw feature usage trends split — hosted API workloads continue to grow but dedicated requests are more predictable for enterprise. Private uptake is fine but slower.
[01:35] Leila: Right, and the financials reflect that. We missed ARR motion targets this quarter and that changes how we think about hiring. I want us to be explicit: we're moving to a temporary hiring pause except for mission-critical roles we sign off.
[02:05] Owen: I know that will cause worry. We'll be working to protect critical paths and to support managers on messaging. we'll still fill essential SRE and security roles.
[02:26] Priya: For customer success, the ask is to be transparent with our top deals — show them roadmaps and where we can commit to reliability SLAs. That helps conversion.
[02:50] Leila: Agreed. Also we need a clear narrative for customers around latency vs cost — the variables that matter when they choose dedicated capacity vs hosted.
[03:14] Anonymous (Speaker 7): Quick question on runway — do we have time to push a large private deployment sale before Q4? Or do we need to re-align expectations?
[03:35] Leila: Short answer: we have runway but it's tighter. we need higher conviction deals, and some deals are longer sales cycles. we'll prioritize pipeline and shift focus to mid-market where cycle is shorter.
[04:05] Sanjay: Technical note: private deployments still need more automation — the onboarding friction is a gating factor on conversion. we can invest in that but it's a medium lead time.
[04:30] Marco: So the tradeoff is clear: keep investing in Private to win the enterprise long-term or accelerate productization of Dedicated to close faster at predictable unit economics. We can't do both fully.
[05:00] Rachel: leaning towards a split approach: small team to unblock Private onboarding (automation + docs), while productizing a high-value Dedicated offering that addresses top customer needs (KV cache mem, easier quantization profiles).
[05:28] Leila: I like that. We also need to fix morale — there's a lot of anxiety. Owen, can you speak to the people plan?
[05:40] Owen: We're framing messages for managers, offering 1:1s, and looking at temporary contractor support for SRE to relieve load. Also planning an all-hands Q&A next week for role-specific questions.
[06:05] Leila: Ok. On reliability, Marco, Sanjay — I want a tangible set of measures we can show to customers: mean recovery time, rollback frequency, and a simple incident summary for the last 6 months.
[06:30] Marco: We'll have a two-page runbook and an incident TL;DR that can be customer-facing. I'll own that.
[06:45] Sanjay: We'll add performance benchmark docs, include sequence-length-specific latency curves and token-cost tradeoffs.
[07:05] Rachel: We'll also adjust product comms so sales can quickly explain tradeoffs to customers, and we'll provide a 'Guides for Choosing' playbook: hosted -> dedicated -> private with decision points.
[07:32] Leila: Great. Now open to questions. please try to be succinct.
[07:45] Speaker 9: Are we changing comp or bonuses because of the miss?
[07:50] Leila: No immediate changes to comp today. We will look at performance carefully — but we want to avoid knee-jerk reactions.
[08:10] Speaker 10: On the hiring freeze, what counts as mission-critical?
[08:15] Owen: Security, SRE, and a handful of customer-facing roles tied to signed deals. We'll route requests through the leadership triage.
[08:35] Marco: On the SRE load, a lot of the pain is on-call handover and signal-to-noise in alerts. Short term we can triage with contractors but we need better alerting/slo tuning.
[09:02] Sanjay: I'd like an executive-level SLO dashboard, even if minimal, so exec and sales can speak to customers with numbers not promises.
[09:20] Leila: Good ask. Rachel, can product help define 3 top SLOs that map to customer asks?
[09:30] Rachel: Yes — P50/P95 latencies for short and long sequences, token cost per 1k tokens by model family, and availability per region.
[09:48] Speaker 12: Security/compliance — where are we on SOC2 and ISO? Customers are asking.
[09:55] Priya: SOC 2 in progress, control mapping done, auditors in May. ISO start scheduled for Q3. We need an updated security kit for sales now.
[10:12] Leila: Ok that goes to Priya as action item.
[10:18] Speaker 13 (Slight crosstalk): a quick ask — can we lower the barrier for trialing models with constrained budgets? If we tighten credit limits it hurts discovery.
[10:34] Rachel: We can propose a short-term promotion for startups and dev teams, but must guard against abuse. We'll draft criteria.
[10:52] Leila: Let's keep momentum. Agenda shift: quick lightning updates from functional leads. Marco, 90 seconds.
[11:00] Marco: Engineering is stabilizing the inference runtime, focusing on kernel scheduling fixes and batching heuristics. We'll roll a small patch next week and monitor.
[11:28] Sanjay: Research is experimenting with quantization modes that preserve quality for larger context windows at lower token cost — early results promising but more evals needed.
[11:46] Rachel: Product will freeze new feature work for two weeks while we triage roadmap priorities; we'll maintain work on must-have Dedicated features.
[12:05] Priya: CS is prioritizing three named accounts for Q2 — doing tailored benchmarks and SLA proposals.
[12:20] Owen: People: focusing on manager coaching and immediate mental-health resources; rolling out a small stipend for therapist sessions and extra comp time.
[12:40] Speaker 15: Question about pricing — are we going to adjust list pricing to better communicate discounts on volume?
[12:46] Leila: We will not do major list price changes today, but we will provide clearer tiered pricing examples that show cost per token at volume and for dedicated pools. Sales will get a pricing cheat sheet.
[13:10] Leila: Ok, last block: open mic for 20 minutes. please keep it constructive.
[13:30] Speaker 17: Anyone worried about burnout? we had three nights with on-call spikes last month.
[13:38] Marco: We saw that — and the pattern is overlapping maintenance windows and a small ops team. The temporary contractors should help.
[13:58] Owen: We'll also institute protected no-meeting blocks for anyone on a rotation to recover the next day.
[14:15] Speaker 19: Will the hiring pause hit IC career ladders?
[14:20] Owen: Promotions still happen; compensation reviews are separate. The pause is about new headcount.
[14:35] Leila: Final thoughts — this is a period of tightening and focus. We'll be more transparent with metrics, and leadership is accountable for clear comms. We'll share a follow-up email with specifics.
[14:50] Leila: Thanks all. Meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcript quality: transcription includes occasional name misrecognitions and punctuation errors. Some low-volume attendees were labeled as generic speakers.
